scenarios.description: Unauthenticated traffic must not mutate authenticated dedup authority.

provenance.sourceTest: Phase 0.4 admission-order audit; newly discovered forged-then-valid regression

given: a signed-required packet identity whose canonical packet identifier is stable
a forged packet followed by the valid packet with the same dedup identity
when: the valid packet subsequently enters admission
then: the forged packet does not enter authenticated dedup authority
the valid packet is admitted exactly once

scenarios.description: A peer-ID change must not create a new authenticated identity or contact.
given: an old PeerId and a newly announced PeerId bound by valid authenticated evidence
when: the peer rotates or replaces its ephemeral PeerId
then: the old PeerId is retained only as bounded historical evidence

scenarios.description: Reconnect creates a new link fact without duplicating peer, identity, or contact authority.
given: an authenticated peer observed on LinkId A
when: LinkId A disconnects and the same peer reconnects on LinkId B
then: LinkId B is distinct from LinkId A
PeerId, AuthenticatedIdentityId, and ContactId are not reconstructed from the link identifier

scenarios.description: Multiple simultaneous links may provide evidence for one identity without becoming identity keys.
given: LinkId A and LinkId B both authenticate to one static identity
then: routing policy can choose a link without rewriting identity or contact state

scenarios.description: Future static-key rotation must require explicit authenticated evidence and must not be inferred from peer or link churn.
given: a ContactId bound to an existing AuthenticatedIdentityId
when: a new static identity claims continuity
then: LinkId and PeerId changes alone cannot authorize rotation
the new AuthenticatedIdentityId remains separate until continuity evidence is verified
ContactId continuity follows explicit product policy
